scope: SIGSTOP during a real mutating installation command, with three native full service processes and two real systemd nodes
checks: instance UUID mapped to its owned Popen by observing registration before/after startup
stopped owner removed from load-balancer backends; cleanup resumes only owned stopped processes
unrelated node completed before original lease expiry
database-time expiry led to durable failed/blocked work without original payload replay
busy remote receiver refused positive proof and kept resource blocked
remote completion receipt fenced by explicit recheck while old process remained stopped
resumed old process heartbeat observed; original operation and progress/event counts unchanged
original job remained failed until an independent linked retry completed
remote daemon-reload count exactly one for original and two after legitimate retry
complete existing two-node CA/authorization/quota/intermediate-CA/deployment/uninstall workflow after process recovery
limits: This specifically proves indeterminate remote work recovery; database-only automatic takeover still needs separate real-process coverage.
Diagnostic sampling is bounded and cannot prove the absence of sub-sample lock waits or constitute a fair performance comparison.
The first pre-fix matrix hit an intermittent pool timeout; earlier/final positive runs and targeted fixes do not establish universal capacity.
